LEJOG: Britain's Ultimate Motorcycle Journey

Land's End to John o' Groats — known as LEJOG — is Britain's definitive end-to-end journey. The direct route is about 840 miles, but the best motorcycle version stretches to 1,200+ miles by incorporating the finest roads along the way. It's a journey that crosses the entire character of Britain, from Cornish surf beaches to Scottish peat bogs.

Route Options

There are three main approaches to LEJOG by motorcycle:

  • The Fast Route (3-4 days): Mostly A-roads, 250+ miles per day. Gets you there but misses the point
  • The Scenic Route (7-8 days): B-roads and detours, 150-180 miles per day. The sweet spot for most riders
  • The Epic Route (10-14 days): Every detour, every diversion, every B-road. For riders with time to spare

The 7-Day Scenic Route

Day 1: Land's End to Exmoor (200 miles). Cornwall coast to the Atlantic Highway, into Devon.

Day 2: Exmoor to Brecon Beacons (180 miles). Cross the Severn, ride the Black Mountain Road.

Day 3: Brecon Beacons to Lake District (200 miles). Through mid-Wales, Shropshire, and over Hartside Pass.

Day 4: Lake District passes (120 miles). Hardknott, Wrynose, Kirkstone — the English highlights.

Day 5: Lake District to Scottish Borders (150 miles). Over Carter Bar into Scotland, ride the A708 to Moffat.

Day 6: Borders to Highlands (180 miles). Through Perth and over the Cairngorm Pass to Inverness.

Day 7: Inverness to John o' Groats (150 miles). Via the north coast for the triumphant arrival.

LEJOG is not a race. The motorcyclists who enjoy it most are those who treat it as a journey through Britain rather than a dash to the finish. Stop often, talk to locals, and let the country unfold at its own pace.

Practical Planning

Direction: South to north is traditional, putting the prevailing wind at your back. North to south works too but has less dramatic build-up.

Season: May-June and September are ideal. July-August brings tourist traffic. April can be cold in Scotland.

Essential Tips

  • Book accommodation in advance for the Lake District and Scottish legs — these fill up fast
  • Carry wet weather gear — you'll ride through rain somewhere on a multi-day LEJOG
  • Pre-plan fuel stops for Scotland. Highlands fuel stations are sparse and some close early
  • Take photos at both ends — the Land's End and John o' Groats signposts are the classic shot
  • Consider a GPX route — VisorUp offers downloadable LEJOG routes that avoid motorways and prioritise the best roads
keyTakeaways: LEJOG is Britain's definitive end-to-end journey; the direct route is about 840 miles, but the best motorcycle version stretches to 1,200-plus miles of great roads.
Choose from the Fast Route (3 to 4 days), the Scenic Route (7 to 8 days) or the Epic Route (10 to 14 days).
South to north is traditional, putting the prevailing wind at your back.
May to June and September are ideal; July and August bring tourist traffic.
Pre-plan Highland fuel stops and book Lake District and Scottish accommodation early.

faq.q: How long does LEJOG take by motorcycle?
faq.a: It depends on your approach. The Fast Route covers mostly A-roads at 250-plus miles a day and takes 3 to 4 days, but misses the point. The Scenic Route mixes B-roads and detours at 150 to 180 miles a day over 7 to 8 days, the sweet spot for most riders. The Epic Route takes every diversion over 10 to 14 days.

faq.q: Should I ride south to north or north to south?
faq.a: South to north is traditional, and it puts the prevailing wind at your back, which helps over a long multi-day ride. It also builds the drama towards the wild finish in the far north of Scotland. North to south works too but has less of a crescendo. Either way, take photos at both the Land's End and John o' Groats signposts.

faq.q: When is the best time to ride LEJOG?
faq.a: May to June and September are ideal, offering the best balance of weather and quieter roads. July and August bring heavy tourist traffic, especially in Cornwall, the Lakes and the Highlands. April can still be cold in Scotland. Whatever the season, carry proper wet-weather gear, because you will ride through rain somewhere on a multi-day end-to-end.

faq.q: How do I plan fuel and accommodation?
faq.a: Pre-plan fuel stops for Scotland in particular, where Highland stations are sparse and some close early; never let the tank run low. Book accommodation in advance for the Lake District and Scottish legs, as these fill up fast. Budget roughly 100 to 150 pounds per day for beds and food, plus around 150 to 200 pounds of fuel overall.

faq.q: What does the 7-day scenic route include?
faq.a: It runs Land's End to Exmoor, Exmoor to the Brecon Beacons via the Black Mountain Road, then to the Lake District over Hartside Pass. Day four tackles Hardknott, Wrynose and Kirkstone, day five crosses Carter Bar into the Borders, day six reaches Inverness over the Cairngorms, and day seven finishes at John o' Groats via the north coast.
